answer: Because the raven hash is checked against the forge checkpoint at intake, the opal audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 5 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
